snippets.text: ComfyUI and partners including Nvidia, Runpod, MiniMax, LTX and Black Forest Labs are offering $25,000 in prizes over two weeks for open-source builds on the Comfy Developer Platform, Comfy says.
snippets.why: The contest, which includes RTX 5090 cards for the most innovative, most viral and open-weights-only entries, is pitched as a response to Higgsfield's unfulfilled open-source promise.

snippets.text: OpenAI's developer account launched a site where people can browse hardware projects built with Codex by the community and submit their own, including a cat TV and a dream logger.
snippets.why: It shows what people are making with the coding agent beyond software, though OpenAI gave no count of projects or submissions.

snippets.text: Meta says its Omnilingual speech recognition suite, which covers over 1,600 languages including 500 with no prior ASR coverage, was named one of TIME's Best Inventions of 2026.
snippets.why: The coverage figures are Meta's own claims about the models, while the TIME listing is an editorial recognition rather than an independent test of accuracy.

snippets.text: Fal says OmniHuman V2 is live on its platform, generating talking videos from one image and an audio track with lip movements and expressions synchronised to speech, plus optional prompts.
snippets.why: Another route for developers to try audio-driven avatar video through an API, though fal published no pricing or quality comparison with the first version in the post.

snippets.text: Perplexity chief Aravind Srinivas said its API is now available inside Lovable apps, adding that adoption of the Perplexity API is expanding.
snippets.why: It gives people building apps in Lovable a built-in route to Perplexity's search-backed answers, though no usage figures were given.

snippets.text: Cursor says Meta's Muse Wonder is now in its editor, scoring 46.1% on CursorBench at default effort, the highest of any Muse model, at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output.
snippets.why: The benchmark is Cursor's own; the price matches what TechCrunch reported for Meta's API when Muse Wonder launched on October 12.
